territorial_scope.description: Michigan state statute; injunctive actions are brought in Michigan circuit courts, in the county of a party's residence or where the media could influence electors in an upcoming election.

evidence.quote: The circuit court for the county in which the materially deceptive media at issue could deceive and influence electors in an upcoming election.

summary.short: Adds section 932f to Michigan's Election Law. Bars any person from distributing AI-produced media that falsely depicts an individual within 90 days before an election, with intent to harm a candidate or deceive electors, unless a disclaimer is included. Sets misdemeanor and felony penalties and allows injunctive relief.
summary.long: Adds section 932f to the Michigan Election Law (1954 PA 116). Prohibits knowingly distributing, or agreeing to distribute, AI-produced image, audio or video that falsely depicts an individual, within 90 days before an election, when intended to harm a candidate or deceive electors and reasonably likely to do so. A disclaimer stating that the media was manipulated by technical means, with placement and size rules by media type, takes the media outside the prohibition; edited media must cite the original source. A first violation is a misdemeanor (up to 90 days' imprisonment or a $500 fine, or both); a violation within five years of a previous conviction is a felony (up to 5 years or a $1,000 fine, or both). The attorney general, depicted individuals, injured candidates and organizations representing likely-deceived voters may seek permanent injunctive relief in specified circuit courts. The plaintiff must prove knowledge by clear and convincing evidence, frivolous complaints are dismissed, and preliminary injunctions are barred. The act takes effect only if House Bill 5143 of the 102nd Legislature is enacted.

obligations.summary: A person may not distribute, or agree with another person to distribute, materially deceptive media (AI-produced image, audio or video falsely depicting an individual) where the person knows it falsely represents the depicted individual, distribution occurs within 90 days before an election, and the person intends harm to a candidate's reputation or prospects or to deceive electors, with distribution reasonably likely to cause that result. Does not apply where the disclaimer conditions in subsection (2) are met. Enacting section 1 makes the amendment conditional on enactment of House Bill 5143 of the 102nd Legislature.
obligations.conditional_on: All of the subsection (1)(a)-(d) conditions must hold jointly; subsection (2) exemption not met; Enacting section 1: takes effect only if House Bill No. 5143 of the 102nd Legislature is enacted into law.

evidence.quote: a person shall not distribute, or enter into an agreement with another person to distribute, materially deceptive media

obligations.summary: To fall outside the subsection (1) prohibition, the person's media must carry a disclaimer that it has been manipulated by technical means and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur, meeting format requirements for video, audio-only, and image media (placement, visibility, size, language). Edited media must also include a citation to the original unedited source. Applies only where the person relies on this exemption.
obligations.conditional_on: Operates only as a condition of the subsection (2) exemption from the subsection (1) prohibition, and only if the media is distributed as described in subsection (1).

evidence.quote: The media includes a disclaimer informing the viewer that the media has been manipulated by technical means and depicts speech or conduct that did not occur.
